_comment: Adminwright review rules for Alibaba Open Code Review. Passed via --rule (code_review.py does this by default). Schema: rules[] with path (glob, first match wins) and rule (reviewer instructions); exclude[] never reviewed. A matching custom rule REPLACES the system language rules for that file, so every rule below starts by asking for the normal language review. Rules instruct the reviewer; deterministic enforcement lives in tests and release gates. Adjust the globs to the project's layout when it differs.

rules.rule: Apply your normal thorough review for this file's language and framework first. Then check the admin-console contract: every mutation handler enforces server-side authorization with default deny — client-side checks and hidden navigation count for nothing; authorization validates both the action and the object/tenant scope per request; bulk operations authorize per target row and report per-item results; every mutation, and every privileged read where policy requires, emits a tamper-evident audit event with actor, target, time, reason, correlation id, result, and safe before/after values; financial, messaging, provisioning, and integration commands are idempotent; destructive actions require preview, confirmation, reason capture, step-up authentication, or approval proportional to risk; secrets and raw regulated data never appear in logs, errors, URLs, or audit payloads.
